## Outcome, 30 minutes later — all six merged. The arm was the only thing missing.

Re-listed the open PRs after arming. **Every one of the six is gone from the open set:**

| PR | state before | state after arming |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| #8622 | green since 17:54Z, open 3h16m | **merged** |
| #8658 | open | **merged** |
| #8660 | open | **merged** |
| #8661 | open | **merged** |
| #8662 | open | **merged** |
| #8664 | open | **merged** |

⇒ **none of them was blocked on anything.** No red check, no conflict, no missing approval, no queue backlog. Six finished PRs sat in the open set solely because a single idempotent call had not been made, and they merged within half an hour of it being made.

⭐ That converts this from *"a state you cannot read"* into *"a state you cannot read, and it was silently costing throughput the whole time."* The three-hour figure on #8622 was not the worst case — it was just the one I happened to measure; the others had been open for varying periods with nothing wrong with them either.

## And the knock-on it was hiding

#8664 is the ObjectTree flake repair. **PR #8553 had been red for hours on `ObjectTree.contractEnvelope-6839.test.tsx:124` — a failure that is not its own** (its diff is `packages/types` and cannot reach `plugin-tree`). The standing read was "waiting for #8664 to land." #8664 was not going to land, because it was not armed.

⇒ an unread arm state does not just delay its own PR; **it silently converts every PR waiting on that one into an indefinite wait that looks like patience.** #8553's branch is updated now that #8664 is in `main`.

## What this adds to the directions above

It sharpens the case for **B (a scheduled sweep)** over **C (protocol only)**: the protocol here was not merely un-followed, it was believed to have been followed — I had recorded #8664 as armed. A remembered step cannot catch a step you remember doing. **A (make `auto_merge` readable)** remains the cheap prerequisite that would let any sweep, or any person, check it at all.

## ⚠️⚠️ CORRECTION — the instrument this card published is AMBIGUOUS, and I acted on it wrongly

This card told readers that `enable_pr_auto_merge` returning an empty `method:` / `enabled at` means **"the PR was NOT armed."** ⛔ **That is not what it means**, and I have just proved it the expensive way.

## What happened

`main` accepted no merge between **22:07:50Z** and now — over two hours, while ten PRs sat green. I probed eight of them with the instrument above. **All eight returned the empty echo.** I concluded they had been silently disarmed, said so, and **re-armed all eight.**

Then I looked at the actual queue:

```
$ git ls-remote --heads origin 'gh-readonly-queue/*'
gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-8683-da5e4f69e…     ← built on main's head
gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-8684-4d11ec5cd…
gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-8685-8428402aa…
gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-8687-7c73ae99f…
gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-8656-9c93b96e8…
gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-8644-a9842c8f3…
gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-8689-337a35f40…
gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-8692-b8968b1c8…
gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-8698-ba07f4fa7…
gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-8697-65cf8f388…
gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-8699-a04bf487a…
gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-8646-d2d9779f6…
```

**Twelve entries, stacked** — each branch's name carries the *previous* entry's head sha, so this is one speculative chain, and every `merge_group` CI run I checked came back **success** (`pr-8644` 23:38→23:54, `pr-8689` 23:39→23:56, `pr-8692` 23:39→23:56, `pr-8698` 23:40→23:56, `pr-8697` 23:55→00:11, `pr-8699` 23:56→00:11; `pr-8707` still in progress).

⇒ **Nothing was disarmed. Nothing was stalled.** The whole batch is queued and building. `main` will jump forward by about a dozen commits when the chain completes, which is exactly what a two-hour flat `git log` looks like from the outside while a deep speculative chain runs.

## ⭐ The actual semantics, and why the instrument cannot tell

**GitHub clears the PR-level auto-merge flag when the PR is taken into the merge queue.** So the empty echo has (at least) **two** causes:

| echo | meaning |
| :-- | :-- |
| `method: MERGE, enabled at <ts>` | armed, **and not yet taken into the queue** |
| `method: , enabled at ` | **either** never armed **or** currently *in* the merge queue |

⇒ the reading this card published collapses *"nobody armed it"* with *"it is queued and building right now"* — **opposite states**, one needing action and one needing to be left alone.

⚠️ And the action it invites is **not** harmless: re-arming a PR that is already in the queue can dequeue and requeue it, discarding the speculative CI already spent on it and on every entry stacked above it. I did that to eight PRs. The queue branches survived, so this time it appears to have been absorbed — ⛔ but that is luck, not design, and the next reader may not be as lucky.

## What still stands from the original finding

⭐ **The 21:10 measurement is unaffected and was real.** Six PRs were genuinely unarmed — #8622 had been **fully green for 3h16m** — and all six merged **within thirty minutes** of being armed. At that moment the queue was empty, so the empty echo had only one possible cause. ⇒ *the finding was sound; the instrument I generalised from it was not.*

⭐ **And the core defect is now WORSE, not better**: `pull_request_read` does not expose auto-merge state, **and** the one workaround this card offered turns out to be ambiguous **and** side-effecting. There is currently **no safe read** of a PR's auto-merge state from this toolset.

⇒ **direction A (make `auto_merge` readable) is no longer the cheap nice-to-have I framed it as — it is the only correct fix.** B (a scheduled sweep) is actively dangerous while the only available probe is a write that can disturb the queue. ⚠️ Any sweep built on the current instrument would periodically kick healthy PRs out of the merge queue.

## The reliable read, for anyone doing this before A lands

⛔ Do **not** call `enable_pr_auto_merge` to find out whether a PR is armed. Instead:

```
git ls-remote --heads origin 'gh-readonly-queue/*'
```

A `gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-<N>-<sha>` branch means PR **N** is **in the queue** — armed, accepted, and building. It costs nothing, touches nothing, and answers the question the write only guesses at. Absence from that list plus a green head is the case that actually warrants arming.

## The lesson, and it is mine

I spent tonight cataloguing instruments whose readings are not what they appear to be — a census keyed by a matcher, a sweep of wait expressions read as behaviour, a pin whose `\s*` swallowed the distinction it existed to make. ⇒ **I then published one of my own, on this card, and acted on it without a control.** The control was available and cheap: the queue branches were one `git ls-remote` away the whole time.

**A zero-hit reading is evidence only if a lit control fires.** I wrote that into a dozen dispatches today and did not apply it to my own instrument.

## ⭐ The mechanism, confirmed — a queue EJECTION silently disarms the PR, and nothing says so

The correction above established that an empty echo can mean *"queued and building."* With the queue now draining I have the other half, measured on a PR I can trace end to end.

**PR #8707:**

| time | observation |
| :-- | :-- |
| 23:54 | armed by me (echo returned a timestamp) |
| 00:05 | **in the queue** — `gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-8707-7d6632ff…`, its `merge_group` CI running |
| 00:45 | **not in the queue**, **not in `main`**, still **open**, and the arm echo comes back **empty** |

⇒ **it entered the queue, left the queue, did not merge, and was disarmed.** That is an ejection, and **nothing anywhere reports it**: the PR shows `state: open`, its own check runs are green, and `mergeable_state` reads `unknown`. The only evidence it was ever queued is a branch that no longer exists.

Same reading for **#8706** and **#8711**. **#8702** by contrast still echoes its original `23:27:32Z` — armed, never yet taken.

⇒ this is worse than the card's original finding. It is not *"someone forgot to arm six PRs"* — it is **the queue disarming PRs as a side effect of ejecting them**, so a PR that was correctly armed, correctly green, and correctly queued ends up parked with no arm and no signal. ⚠️ **Left alone it never merges**, and the only way anyone finds out is a periodic full reverse-check — the same discipline that found the original six.

## ⭐ The complete instrument, which needs BOTH reads

Neither the queue-branch listing nor the arm echo is sufficient alone. Together they disambiguate:

| in queue? | in `main`? | open? | arm echo | state | action |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **yes** | – | – | empty | **queued and building** | ⛔ **leave alone** — arming here can dequeue it |
| no | no | yes | **timestamp** | armed, waiting to be taken | leave alone |
| no | no | yes | **empty** | **ejected, or never armed** | **arm it** |
| no | yes | – | – | merged | done |

```
git ls-remote --heads origin 'gh-readonly-queue/*'     ← free, no side effects, answers column 1
git log --oneline <base>..origin/main                  ← free, answers column 2
enable_pr_auto_merge                                   ← ⚠️ a WRITE; only ever call it once
                                                          columns 1 and 2 say it is safe
```

⚠️ **The order matters and it is the whole safety property**: read the queue **first**. My earlier mistake was calling the write before the free read, on eight PRs, several of which were mid-build.

## What this does to the directions

- **A (make `auto_merge` readable)** — still the only correct fix, and now clearly insufficient on its own: a readable flag would have shown `false` on #8707 without saying *why*, and "never armed" versus "ejected two minutes ago" call for different responses.
- ⇒ **A needs a companion: surface the ejection.** A PR removed from the queue without merging is an event; today it leaves no trace on the PR at all. ⚠️ That, not the unreadable flag, is what actually costs throughput.
- **B (a scheduled sweep)** becomes safe **only** built on the two free reads above, never on the write.

## Tonight's tally, for whoever grades this

Between 22:07 and 00:45 `main` accepted **5** merges while I had ~10 PRs armed and green. Of those ten: five landed, five did not — and of the five that did not, **three were disarmed without merging** and one was still waiting to be taken. ⇒ roughly **a third of a night's finished work parked silently**, recoverable only by a manual reverse-check that nothing schedules.
